checks.basis: Read the specified repository/game/art/architecture/enemies/weapons documents. Current diff against base 24bb855f4 is two client files, 11 additions. CombatFeel.onEnemyDied requires nativeDeath, reuses existing flash/ripple and prior health for conservative presentation heat, beside unchanged death sound. Both changed files, game_world.ts and triangle_fracture.ts are byte-identical at original capture 4e0482e13 and current 850b70e3b; working tree tracked diff empty.

Initial 199 and supplementary 273 raw RGBA hashes match metadata; every native PNG RGB matches raw RGB. All four MP4 hashes match their metadata and CPU decode succeeded. Initial all native full frames and every decoded ROI frame were inspected. Supplement every native and decoded ROI frame was inspected consecutively at 1:1, with exact full-context sampling recorded separately. The onset/restored standalone PNGs are byte-identical to control f21/candidate f19/f24.

Supplement receipts contain exactly two delivered normal input actions, no pending actions: ADS rifle hold/shoot and release when nativeDeath is observed. Accepted logs show player-2 body hits reaching zero: candidate soldier-e3 108/88/68/48/28/8/0; control soldier-e8 109/89/69/49/29/9/0. Health snapshots, ammo 30 to 23, roster removal and same-id nativeDeath correlate. Acquisition used invincibility/timescale4, then normal time. Actual accepted events do not call VFX, mesh, death or timer manipulation.

Candidate soldier-e3 nativeDeath first observed f19 at wall 0.961891 s, sim 45325, non-original mesh and activeParts=1. Same actor stays non-original f19-23, then original f24 at 1.215235 s, sim 45605, activeParts=0; all later death samples through f92 remain original. Observed 280 simulation ms to first restored sample is consistent with nominal 260 ms under discrete sampling, not an exact expiry measurement. Supplement control soldier-e8 first death f21 original and all death samples through f98 original. Counts 4/4 and 1/1 ending activeParts=0 support cleanup; they are not the attachment proof.

Initial second kill native f38-40 / decoded f63-67 provides the clearest fine white localized chest/forearm triangle signature, with helmet/face, red sleeve, equipment and rifle retaining native detail. Supplement candidate f19 / decoded f29-30 exposes a small white chest-side terminal patch distinct from the red screen-space kill marker; surrounding helmet/clothing/equipment retain color and form. No body-wide white wash, screen-wide terminal debris or replacement of the native character by a proxy was observed. ADS/range/marker occlusion limits precise patch-shape comparison.

Supplement native f19-23 and decoded f29-35 were inspected individually. The exposed patch remains localized on the visible body during the early bend; no detached patch/weapon, T-pose or gross silhouette break was observed in unoccluded pixels. Original mesh return at native f24 / decoded f36 retains a coherent helmet, torso, arms and held rifle. Native f24-39 continuing bend and f40-49 seated fall preserve body/weapon relationships, closing the initial offscreen-expiry gap. This is visible coherence of one held-camera soldier death, not certification of every bone or animation pose.

The same soldier remains in view after restoration: native f24-39 bends/crouches, f40-49 lowers to seated collapse, f50-59 rolls/extends into a horizontal fall, then remains partly visible settled through the late death samples. No gross restoration pop, animation reset, frozen standing corpse or residual white terminal effect was observed in captured frames. NativeDeath remains true after restoration through f92; actor absent at f93. Initial control native f47-60 shows its original-mesh forward fall with held rifle; supplementary control corpse is obscured and is not claimed as a pixel-matched motion comparison.

Changed source does not alter authoritative damage, weapon rules, audio, native death animation/timing, rig/assets/shader, v0.28 ADS/recoil, spawns or stream/TTS fiction. Ordinary ADS firing/recoil/ammo and input release remain visible. World/native weapon detail, flat LiveTube cards and game-fiction cheat presentation stay distinct in inspected context. Fair hidden spawning passes unchanged-source and initial fixture scope only; this is not an exhaustive spawning or viewer-feature audit.

limitations: Scope is the two-file lethal presentation change and supplied ordinary rifle deaths. ALL PASS is not a whole-game, every-character/every-angle, performance, renderer-health or audible-quality certification. Four candidate kills provide terminal evidence; only one supplementary candidate kill provides held-view restoration/follow-through.

Initial evidence retains actual capture candidate 4e0482e13 on bfce057de, before merged viewer pulse. It is not relabeled 850b70e3b. Supplement captures use 850b70e3b and control bfcb267 whose tracked tree equals merged base 24bb855f4. Four scoped source-file hashes are identical between original capture and rebase.

Requested seed 0C0FFEE1 does not produce pixel-matched camera/actors/locations. Initial lock ranges are control 4.088 m and candidate 6.279 m. Supplement control 8.058518 m and candidate 9.498434 m. Supplement control explicitly aimAt body on firing onset; candidate retains its acquired aim target. These differences preclude precise pixel/pose parity or effect-size comparison.

Supplementary control soldier-e8 corpse is hidden by sights/wall in inspected context. Its original-mesh/death claim is correlated telemetry/log evidence, not direct visible-collapse evidence. Initial control supplies the visible original-mesh native-death comparison. No claim that a visible nearby live actor is the killed control target.

Candidate ADS sights and red kill marker obscure part of the terminal patch; effect visible in exposed body pixels, not every pixel. Later player weapon partly hides torso/rifle during horizontal fall. Held-rifle continuity is visible across restoration and early collapse, not fully visible through final despawn.

Existing ripple anchor follows actor root translation/yaw rather than individual animated bones; the post-death mark probe skips removed snapshot actors. No gross attachment defect was observed in the held sample, but this does not establish bone-perfect patch anchoring for unobserved falls/angles. Aggregate counters alone were not used to clear the attachment gate.

All captured frames inspected does not mean every engine-rendered instant was captured. Supplement native gaps: candidate mean 51.391151 ms, max 230.367 ms, 43 target intervals missed; control mean 44.798703 ms, max 228.191 ms, 20 missed. Candidate f18-to-f19 onset gap 86.763 ms; subsequent f19-to-f24 gaps 74.381/43.825/42.962/44.682/47.494 ms. Exact subframe onset/expiry and unrecorded instants cannot be judged. Initial capture gaps remain in the preserved report.

All videos are silent CFR30, holding/dropping actual native images without interpolation; lossy H264 yuv420p affects fine edges/color. Native PNGs govern detail. CPU decode/contact-sheet inspection is frame-by-frame and not continuous 1x playback. All decoded frames were reviewed only inside the specified ROI, not over the entire decoded full frame.

Audio/TTS quality, mixing and audible sync are excluded/unverified: no audio track, no audition. Unchanged source/audio calls support source scope only. Silent clips cannot clear an audible-quality gate.

Accepted initial and supplementary engine logs each have 62 ERROR lines: 20 missing pre-raster vertex-shader pipeline, 20 pipeline.is_null, 20 Invalid Task ID, one NavRegion3D and one NavMap3D shutdown leak. Zero SCRIPT ERROR lines observed. Logs are not clean; shared errors cannot be attributed to this lethal diff from these runs alone. Renderer health remains outside this visual change verdict.
